review_comments.body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Refresh sessions for notification requests**

When a long-lived client sends session-bearing JSON-RPC notifications between normal calls, those requests never reach this refresh: `handle` returns `202` for every body without an `id` before `dispatch_jsonrpc` invokes `valid_mcp_session?` (the existing `notifications/initialized` path does exactly this). Consequently a client can send notifications within every 24-hour interval yet still have the session expire and receive a 404 on its next `tools/list`, so the sliding idle TTL is not refreshed on each use; validate and touch the session before the notification early return as well.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

Full details: Title check

**Explanation** The title "fix(mcp): refresh the MCP session TTL on each use" matches the main change. The PR refreshes the one-day cache TTL of an MCP session each time a request validates it for the same user, as the objectives and file summary describe. The title is specific and short, and it names the primary change. It does not mention the linked issue's broader goal of stopping unconditional invalidation after 24 hours, but it covers the core change.
Full details: Linked Issues check

**Explanation** Only `#5804` is directly linked, and it is open. Its active-session requirement is met. In app/controllers/mcp_controller.rb, valid_mcp_session? now calls write_mcp_session after a successful read, which rewrites mcp:session:<id> with MCP_SESSION_TTL. Each valid request therefore extends the expiry, so an active client does not expire 24h after initialize. The issue requires that forged, tampered, and cross-user IDs still return 404. The read check still returns false when the entry is missing (forged or expired) or when the cached user ID differs from mcp_user.id (cross-user), so those cases still return 404. The new test in test/controllers/mcp_controller_test.rb covers the active case (200 at +20h and +40h) and the idle case (404 after a full TTL). The issue offers a sliding 30-day cache TTL as an acceptable approach that stays cache-dependent. The PR takes a sliding 1-day TTL instead. The issue's expected behavior also mentions cache restarts and evictions. The PR does not address those, and the PR objectives state this limit. Idle sessions longer than one day still expire. Those limits are accepted scope exclusions, not failures of the chosen approach.
Full details: Out of Scope Changes check

**Explanation** The whole-PR diff (merge base e0d9c9c to head b0ac7c1) touches two files. app/controllers/mcp_controller.rb adds write_mcp_session, which centralizes the cache write. handle_initialize and valid_mcp_session? use it. The change is limited to the sliding-expiry behavior. test/controllers/mcp_controller_test.rb adds one test for that behavior. No unrelated changes were found in the reviewed diffs.
